Excessively large headers are usually caused by too many cookies being set for the domain, very long Set-Cookie headers, or server misconfigurations that add redundant headers. Applications that create many session cookies or tracking cookies across subdomains can accumulate headers that exceed the limit.

This is almost always a server-side or cookie management issue that needs to be addressed either by reducing the number of cookies or by fixing server header configuration.

causes.cause: Too many cookies accumulated for the domain
Server setting excessively large cookies
Server misconfiguration adding duplicate headers
Accumulated cookies across many subdomains

symptoms: Site fails to load with headers too big error
Error may appear after prolonged use of a site
Clearing cookies for the site resolves the issue temporarily
Issue gradually returns as new cookies accumulate

fixSteps.title: Clear cookies for the specific site
fixSteps.instruction: Click the lock icon in the address bar > Cookies > see all cookies for the site > Remove all. Alternatively, go to Settings > Privacy > Cookies > See all site data and search for the domain.

fixSteps.title: Clear all cookies and cache
fixSteps.instruction: Go to browser Settings > Privacy > Clear browsing data. Select 'Cookies and other site data' and 'Cached images and files'. This resets all accumulated headers.

fixSteps.title: Try incognito mode
fixSteps.instruction: Open an incognito/private window and visit the site. If it works, the issue is definitely cookie accumulation in your regular session.

fixSteps.title: Report to the website
fixSteps.instruction: If clearing cookies only temporarily fixes the issue, the website has a cookie management problem. Report the issue to their support team.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the website and need help optimizing cookie usage and header sizes.

faq.q: Why do cookies cause this error?
faq.a: Every cookie for a domain is sent in the request headers on every page load. If a site sets many cookies or very large cookies, the combined header size can exceed the browser's limit.

faq.q: Will this error keep coming back after clearing cookies?
faq.a: If the website has a cookie management issue, yes. The fundamental fix needs to come from the website itself reducing its cookie usage. As a user, periodically clearing cookies is the workaround.

title: Too Many Connection Retries
shortDescription: The browser exhausted its maximum number of automatic retry attempts for the failed request.
fullDescription:
ERR_TOO_MANY_RETRIES occurs when the browser has automatically retried a failed request multiple times and all attempts have failed. The browser gives up after exceeding its internal retry limit rather than continuing indefinitely.

This error is a catch-all that appears after other underlying errors (like connection resets, timeouts, or authentication failures) have occurred repeatedly. The root cause is typically whatever caused the initial failure — the browser tried to work around it by retrying but could not.

This error is particularly common with authentication failures where incorrect credentials cause repeated 401 responses, or with sites that have SSL configuration issues causing repeated handshake failures.

causes.cause: Repeated authentication failures with incorrect credentials
Server consistently rejecting connections
SSL handshake repeatedly failing
Network instability causing repeated connection drops

symptoms: Page fails after extended loading with too many retries error
May see brief authentication prompts before the error
Error takes longer to appear than typical connection errors
Other sites load normally

fixSteps.title: Check your credentials
fixSteps.instruction: If the site requires login, ensure you are using the correct username and password. Repeated wrong credentials trigger retry limits.

fixSteps.title: Clear saved credentials for the site
fixSteps.instruction: Go to browser Settings > Passwords. Search for the affected site and delete any saved passwords. Then try logging in fresh.

fixSteps.title: Clear browser data and restart
fixSteps.instruction: Clear all browsing data including cookies and cache. Close and reopen the browser. Try accessing the site again.

fixSteps.title: Wait and try later
fixSteps.instruction: If the server is under heavy load or experiencing issues, wait 15-30 minutes and try again. The server may have temporarily rate-limited your connection.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after clearing credentials and the site should be accepting your login, the server administrator may need to check their authentication system.

faq.q: How many retries does the browser attempt?
faq.a: The exact number varies by browser and request type, but typically 3-5 retries for connection failures and 2-3 for authentication failures before giving up.

faq.q: Can this error lock me out of a site?
faq.a: The browser error itself does not lock you out, but the repeated failed authentication attempts that caused it might trigger the server's account lockout policy.

title: Network Socket Not Connected
shortDescription: The browser attempted to use a network socket that is no longer connected.
fullDescription:
ERR_SOCKET_NOT_CONNECTED occurs when the browser tries to send data through a network socket that has been disconnected or was never properly established. Network sockets are the underlying communication channels between the browser and servers, and this error indicates the channel is broken.

This error can happen when a connection is interrupted mid-session, when the browser's socket pool becomes corrupted, or when system-level network changes occur while requests are in progress (like Wi-Fi switching or VPN connecting).

The error is relatively rare and usually resolves with a browser restart. If it persists, it may indicate issues with the system's network stack or the browser's internal socket management.

causes.cause: Network connection interrupted mid-session
Browser socket pool corrupted
VPN or network change occurred during page load
System network stack issue

symptoms: Page loading fails with socket not connected error
Error may appear after network interruption or VPN change
Multiple tabs may fail simultaneously
Restarting the browser often fixes the issue

fixSteps.title: Flush socket pools
fixSteps.instruction: In Chrome, go to chrome://net-internals/#sockets and click 'Flush socket pools'. This forces the browser to create fresh connections.

fixSteps.title: Restart the browser
fixSteps.instruction: Close all browser windows completely and reopen the browser. This resets all network connections and socket pools.

fixSteps.title: Check network connection
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure your network connection is stable. If you recently switched networks or connected/disconnected a VPN, wait for the connection to stabilize.

fixSteps.title: Reset Winsock
fixSteps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as administrator and run: netsh winsock reset. Restart your computer. This resets the Windows socket layer.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after Winsock reset and browser reinstall, there may be a deeper system or driver issue.

faq.a: A socket is an endpoint for communication between two programs over a network. When you visit a website, the browser creates a socket to communicate with the web server. Each connection uses its own socket.

faq.q: Why does restarting the browser fix this?
faq.a: Restarting clears the browser's socket pool and forces it to create fresh connections. The old, broken sockets are discarded and new ones are established.

title: HTTP Method Not Allowed
shortDescription: The server recognizes the request method but does not allow it for the requested resource.
fullDescription:
HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed indicates that the server understands the HTTP method in the request (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, etc.) but the target resource does not support that method. For example, trying to POST data to a URL that only accepts GET requests, or trying to DELETE a resource on a read-only endpoint.

The server should include an Allow header in the response listing the methods that are supported for the resource. This helps developers understand which methods can be used.

This error is usually encountered during web development or API interaction rather than regular browsing. It indicates the client is using the wrong HTTP method for the endpoint, which is a programming error rather than a server malfunction.

causes.cause: Wrong HTTP method used for the API endpoint
Web form submitting via wrong method due to misconfiguration
Server misconfiguration blocking certain methods
Browser extension modifying request methods

symptoms: Form submission fails with 405 error
API calls return 405 status code
Error page may list allowed methods
GET requests work but POST/PUT/DELETE fails

fixSteps.title: Check the correct HTTP method
fixSteps.instruction: View the error details for the 'Allow' header which lists accepted methods. Ensure your request uses one of the listed methods.

fixSteps.title: Try a different method
fixSteps.instruction: If you are manually accessing the URL, try adding or removing parameters. Some URLs respond to GET but not POST, or vice versa.

fixSteps.title: Clear browser data
fixSteps.instruction: Cached redirects or form data can sometimes cause method mismatches. Clear cookies and cache for the site and try again.

fixSteps.title: Check API documentation
fixSteps.instruction: If working with an API, consult the documentation to verify the correct HTTP method and endpoint URL for the operation you are trying to perform.

whenToCallPro: If you are a developer encountering this on your own server, review the server routing configuration. If you are a user, report the issue to the website.

faq.a: The most common are GET (retrieve data), POST (submit data), PUT (update data), DELETE (remove data), PATCH (partial update), HEAD (headers only), and OPTIONS (check capabilities).

faq.q: Why would a server block certain methods?
faq.a: For security. A read-only API should not accept DELETE requests, for example. Servers restrict methods to prevent unintended data modification or deletion.

title: HTTP/2 Server Refused Stream
shortDescription: The HTTP/2 server refused to accept a new stream (request) within the existing connection.
fullDescription:
ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM occurs when a server using HTTP/2 protocol rejects a request stream. HTTP/2 multiplexes multiple requests over a single connection using streams, and the server can refuse individual streams without closing the entire connection.

Servers refuse streams when they are overloaded and cannot handle more concurrent requests, when they have reached their configured maximum concurrent streams limit, or when they want to signal the client to open a new connection.

This error is often transient and resolves on retry, as the server may accept the stream once it finishes processing other requests. It is more common during high-traffic periods or when the server is under heavy load.

causes.cause: Server overloaded and refusing new HTTP/2 streams
Maximum concurrent streams limit reached
Server-side HTTP/2 implementation bug
Load balancer rejecting streams during failover

symptoms: Some resources on a page fail to load while others succeed
Error is intermittent and works on retry
Multiple resources from the same server fail simultaneously
Error more frequent during peak traffic times

fixSteps.title: Refresh the page
fixSteps.instruction: Press F5 to reload. Since this is usually a transient overload issue, the server may accept the streams on the next attempt.

fixSteps.title: Hard refresh with cache clear
fixSteps.instruction: Press Ctrl+Shift+R to force reload bypassing cache. This ensures fresh connections are established.

fixSteps.title: Disable HTTP/2 temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: Go to chrome://flags and search for HTTP/2. Disable it to fall back to HTTP/1.1 which does not use stream multiplexing.

fixSteps.title: Wait and retry
fixSteps.instruction: If the server is overloaded, waiting a few minutes before retrying gives it time to recover and accept new connections.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the server and streams are frequently refused, the HTTP/2 max concurrent streams setting may need tuning.

faq.a: HTTP/2 allows multiple requests and responses to be sent simultaneously over a single connection. Each request/response pair is a 'stream'. This is more efficient than HTTP/1.1 which needs separate connections for each request.

faq.q: Does this error mean the server is down?
faq.a: No. The server is up but temporarily unable to handle more concurrent requests. It is refusing new streams to protect itself from overload, not because it has crashed.

title: SSL Unrecognized Server Name
shortDescription: The server does not recognize the hostname sent in the TLS Server Name Indication (SNI) extension.
fullDescription:
ERR_SSL_UNRECOGNIZED_NAME_ALERT occurs when the server sends a TLS 'unrecognized_name' alert in response to the browser's Client Hello message. This happens because the browser sends the requested hostname via the SNI (Server Name Indication) extension during the TLS handshake, and the server does not have a certificate or configuration for that hostname.

SNI allows a single IP address to host multiple HTTPS websites, each with its own certificate. When the server does not recognize the hostname in the SNI, it cannot select the appropriate certificate and configuration, so it sends this alert.

This is typically a server configuration issue where the virtual host configuration does not match the requested domain name, or the domain was recently added to the server but the web server has not been reloaded.

causes.cause: Server not configured to serve the requested domain
DNS pointing to wrong server IP
Web server not reloaded after adding new virtual host
Wildcard certificate not covering the requested subdomain

symptoms: HTTPS connection fails during initial handshake
Error occurs immediately without page loading
HTTP version of the site may work while HTTPS fails
Other sites on the same server work fine

fixSteps.title: Verify DNS resolution
fixSteps.instruction: Open Command Prompt and run: nslookup yourdomain.com. Verify the IP address matches the expected server. If DNS is pointing to the wrong server, the server will not recognize the domain.

fixSteps.title: Try the www version
fixSteps.instruction: If accessing example.com fails, try www.example.com or vice versa. The server may only be configured for one variation.

fixSteps.title: Clear DNS cache
fixSteps.instruction: Run ipconfig /flushdns in Command Prompt as administrator. If DNS was recently changed, your cache may have the old IP.

fixSteps.title: Contact website administrator
fixSteps.instruction: Report the error to the site administrator. They need to add the correct virtual host configuration for your domain on the server.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the server and need help configuring virtual hosts, SNI, or SSL certificates for multiple domains.

faq.a: Server Name Indication (SNI) is a TLS extension that lets the browser tell the server which hostname it wants to connect to during the initial handshake. This allows one server to host multiple HTTPS sites on a single IP address.

faq.q: Can this error be caused by my browser?
faq.a: Very rarely. This is almost always a server-side configuration issue. The browser is correctly sending the hostname; the server just does not recognize it.

title: Proxy Authentication Required
shortDescription: The proxy server requires authentication credentials before forwarding the request.
fullDescription:
HTTP 407 Proxy Authentication Required is similar to HTTP 401 (Unauthorized) but specifically for proxy servers. The proxy server is requesting that the client authenticate itself with valid credentials before it will forward the request to the destination server.

This status code is commonly encountered in corporate environments where all internet traffic passes through an authenticated proxy. Users must provide their network credentials (often their Windows domain username and password) before the proxy will allow them to browse the internet.

The proxy should include a Proxy-Authenticate header in the response indicating the authentication method it supports (Basic, Digest, NTLM, Negotiate, etc.). The browser typically responds by showing a login dialog.

causes.cause: Proxy requires login credentials not yet provided
Saved proxy credentials expired or changed
Browser not passing Windows credentials to proxy automatically
Proxy authentication timeout requiring re-login

symptoms: Browser shows proxy authentication dialog
All websites blocked until proxy credentials entered
Error occurs after password change on network account
Works after entering credentials but fails again after a while

fixSteps.title: Enter proxy credentials
fixSteps.instruction: When the proxy authentication dialog appears, enter your network username and password. On corporate networks, you may need to use the format DOMAIN\username.

fixSteps.title: Clear saved proxy credentials
fixSteps.instruction: Open Credential Manager from Control Panel. Under 'Windows Credentials', find and remove any saved proxy credentials. Then re-enter fresh credentials when prompted.

fixSteps.title: Update saved credentials after password change
fixSteps.instruction: If you recently changed your network password, the old proxy credentials are invalid. Delete the old saved credentials in Credential Manager and authenticate with your new password.

fixSteps.title: Configure automatic authentication
fixSteps.instruction: In Internet Options > Security > Local intranet > Custom level, ensure 'Automatic logon with current user name and password' is selected. This passes Windows credentials to the proxy automatically.

whenToCallPro: If the proxy keeps rejecting valid credentials, contact your IT department. The proxy configuration or your account permissions may need to be updated.

faq.q: Why does the proxy keep asking for my password?
faq.a: The proxy session may have a timeout. Some proxies require re-authentication periodically. If it happens too frequently, ask your IT department to extend the session timeout.
On managed corporate networks, no. The proxy is a security requirement. On personal networks, you can remove the proxy configuration entirely if you do not need it.

title: Certificate Transparency Compliance Required
shortDescription: The website's SSL certificate does not meet Certificate Transparency requirements enforced by the browser.
fullDescription:
ERR_CERT_TRANSPARENCY_REQUIRED occurs when a website's SSL certificate has not been logged in public Certificate Transparency (CT) logs as required by browser policy. Certificate Transparency is a framework that makes certificate issuance publicly auditable, helping detect fraudulently issued certificates.

Chrome requires all publicly-trusted certificates issued after April 2018 to be logged in CT logs. Certificates must include Signed Certificate Timestamps (SCTs) proving they have been logged. Without these SCTs, Chrome will reject the certificate.

This error typically indicates a misconfigured server that is not including SCTs in the TLS handshake, or a certificate authority that failed to log the certificate properly. It can also occur if the server is not providing the correct certificate chain needed for CT validation.

causes.cause: Certificate issued without being logged to CT logs
Server not providing SCTs via TLS extension or OCSP stapling
Certificate authority CT logging failure
Enterprise CA certificate not exempt from CT requirement

symptoms: Chrome blocks the site with certificate transparency error
Firefox may load the site without error (less strict CT enforcement)
Recently issued or renewed certificates trigger the error
Error cannot be bypassed through advanced options

fixSteps.title: Try a different browser
fixSteps.instruction: Firefox does not enforce Certificate Transparency as strictly as Chrome. Try loading the site in Firefox as a temporary workaround.

fixSteps.title: Check certificate details
fixSteps.instruction: If you can view certificate details, check for Signed Certificate Timestamps (SCTs). Their absence confirms this is a CT compliance issue on the server side.

fixSteps.title: Contact the website administrator
fixSteps.instruction: Report the CT compliance issue. The site administrator needs to ensure their certificate is properly logged and SCTs are included in the TLS handshake.

fixSteps.title: Re-issue the certificate (site owners)
fixSteps.instruction: If you manage the site, re-issue the certificate from your CA. Modern CAs automatically log to CT. Ensure your server is configured to deliver SCTs via the TLS extension or OCSP stapling.

whenToCallPro: If you manage a web server and need help configuring Certificate Transparency compliance or re-issuing certificates with proper CT logging.

faq.a: Certificate Transparency is a public logging system for SSL certificates. Every certificate issued by a trusted CA must be logged, making it possible to detect fraudulently or mistakenly issued certificates.

faq.q: Why does Chrome enforce CT but Firefox does not?
faq.a: Google initiated Certificate Transparency and Chrome enforces it strictly. Firefox has been adopting CT enforcement more gradually and may not yet require it for all certificates.

title: HTTP 300 Multiple Choices
shortDescription: The requested resource has multiple representations and the server needs the client to choose one.
fullDescription:
HTTP 300 Multiple Choices indicates the target resource has more than one representation, each with its own identifier, and the user agent or user must pick one. This is rare in practice because most servers either auto-redirect or use content negotiation.

Browsers usually do not render a 300 visibly; they follow a Location header if present or display the server's HTML body listing options. Developers may see this when inspecting Network tab responses.

causes.cause: Server has multiple versions of the resource (language, format)
Misconfigured content negotiation on server

symptoms: Page shows list of alternative URLs
Browser stays on current page without navigating

fixSteps.title: Click a preferred variant
fixSteps.instruction: If the page lists choices, click the one matching your language or format needs.

fixSteps.title: Check Accept headers
fixSteps.instruction: Developers: verify the Accept-Language and Accept headers your client sends so the server can auto-pick.

whenToCallPro: If you run the server and cannot configure proper content negotiation.

faq.a: No, it is an informational redirection status that asks the client to pick among variants.

title: HTTP 301 Moved Permanently
shortDescription: The requested resource has been permanently moved to a new URL.
fullDescription:
HTTP 301 tells browsers and search engines that the resource has permanently relocated to the URL provided in the Location header. Browsers cache this redirect aggressively and may bypass the original URL on future requests.

This status is commonly used when migrating a site to HTTPS, changing domain names, or restructuring URL paths. If the new URL is wrong, users can get stuck in a cached loop that is difficult to recover from without clearing browser data.

causes.cause: Site moved to new domain or HTTPS
URL structure changed permanently
Incorrect permanent redirect cached by browser

symptoms: Browser automatically navigates to a different URL
Old bookmark now opens new address
Cannot access original URL even after server rollback

fixSteps.title: Update your bookmarks
fixSteps.instruction: Save the new final URL as the bookmark instead of the old one.

fixSteps.title: Clear cached redirects
fixSteps.instruction: If a bad 301 is cached, clear browsing data (cached images and files) for the affected site.

whenToCallPro: If you administer the server and a bad 301 was pushed site-wide.

faq.q: Why can't I go back to the old URL?
faq.a: Browsers cache 301 redirects heavily. Clear cache or use a private window to retry the original URL.

title: HTTP 302 Found (Temporary Redirect)
shortDescription: The resource is temporarily at a different URL; use the original URL for future requests.
fullDescription:
HTTP 302 Found indicates a temporary redirect. The server asks the browser to fetch the resource from a different URL this time, but to keep using the original URL for future requests. Unlike 301, 302 is not cached permanently.

302 is commonly used for login redirects, A/B testing, and regional routing. Problems appear when session cookies or auth tokens are lost across the redirect, leading to redirect loops.

causes.cause: Login or authentication redirect
Temporary server maintenance redirect
Broken session causes redirect loop

symptoms: Automatic jump to another URL
Redirect loop ending in ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS
Login page reappears after signing in

fixSteps.title: Clear site cookies
fixSteps.instruction: Open site settings and clear cookies for the affected domain to break broken session loops.

fixSteps.title: Try incognito mode
fixSteps.instruction: Test in a private window to rule out extensions or stored cookies.

whenToCallPro: If the redirect loop is server-side and you cannot modify the server.

faq.a: Yes for permanent moves - search engines won't transfer ranking. Use 301 for permanent redirects.

title: HTTP 304 Not Modified
shortDescription: The cached version of the resource is still valid; no new content is sent.
fullDescription:
HTTP 304 Not Modified is returned when the browser makes a conditional request (using If-Modified-Since or If-None-Match) and the server confirms the cached copy is still current. No response body is sent, saving bandwidth.

This is normal behavior, not an error. Issues arise only when a 304 is returned incorrectly and the user sees stale content that should have been refreshed.

causes.cause: Normal cache validation
Server returns 304 when content actually changed (bad ETag)

symptoms: Page looks outdated despite updates
DevTools Network tab shows 304 for files you expected to reload

fixSteps.title: Hard refresh
fixSteps.instruction: Press Ctrl+F5 (Cmd+Shift+R on macOS) to force revalidation and bypass the cache.

fixSteps.title: Clear cache
fixSteps.instruction: If hard refresh doesn't help, clear cached images and files in browser settings.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed - only if site-wide caching misconfiguration persists.

faq.a: No, it's a success status meaning your cached copy is up to date.

title: HTTP 307 Temporary Redirect
shortDescription: Temporary redirect that preserves the original HTTP method and body.
fullDescription:
HTTP 307 is like 302 but strictly requires the browser to reuse the original HTTP method. If the original request was POST, the follow-up must also be POST with the same body. This prevents accidental method changes that older 302 implementations allowed.

307 is commonly used by HSTS preloads to force HTTPS without changing POST requests into GETs.

causes.cause: HSTS upgrade from HTTP to HTTPS
Temporary server routing redirect

symptoms: URL switches from http:// to https:// automatically
POST form resubmits to a different endpoint

fixSteps.title: Use the HTTPS URL directly
fixSteps.instruction: Bookmark and share the https:// URL to skip the redirect.

whenToCallPro: Not needed for end users.

faq.a: 307 forbids changing the HTTP method, while 302 implementations historically allowed POST to become GET.

title: HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect
shortDescription: Permanent redirect that preserves the original HTTP method and body.
fullDescription:
HTTP 308 Permanent Redirect indicates the resource is permanently at a new URL, and unlike 301, the browser must preserve the HTTP method. Use this when migrating APIs permanently where POST and PUT semantics must not be changed.

Browsers cache 308 aggressively, similar to 301.

causes.cause: Permanent API endpoint migration
Permanent HTTPS upgrade

symptoms: API calls always rerouted to new URL
Bad 308 cached and persists after server rollback

fixSteps.title: Update bookmarks and API configs
fixSteps.instruction: Change saved URLs to the final destination.

fixSteps.title: Clear cached redirects
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cached 308 by clearing site data if the redirect needs to be reverted.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the server and need to unwind a mistaken 308.

faq.a: Yes, all modern browsers from 2016+ support it.

title: HTTP 402 Payment Required
shortDescription: Reserved status code intended for digital payment systems; used by some APIs to signal a paid resource.
fullDescription:
HTTP 402 Payment Required was reserved for future use and has no standardized meaning. Some modern APIs (Stripe, Shopify) repurpose it to signal that a request cannot proceed until payment is made or a paid plan is upgraded.

End users rarely encounter 402 from a browser directly; it usually appears in API responses inspected via DevTools.

causes.cause: API requires payment or paid subscription upgrade
Billing or payment method expired

symptoms: API call fails with 402 status
Paid feature returns error
Web app shows billing upgrade prompt

fixSteps.title: Check billing status
fixSteps.instruction: Log into the service's billing portal and verify your subscription or payment method.

fixSteps.title: Update payment method
fixSteps.instruction: Add a valid card and retry the request.

whenToCallPro: If the billing is enterprise and requires your account team.

faq.a: It's reserved in the HTTP spec but has no universal meaning; implementations vary by API.

title: HTTP 410 Gone
shortDescription: The requested resource is permanently unavailable with no forwarding address.
fullDescription:
HTTP 410 Gone is like 404 but explicitly tells clients and search engines the resource has been intentionally removed and will not return. Search engines drop 410 URLs from their index faster than 404s.

Users see 410 when a page, product, or article has been deliberately retired.

causes.cause: Content deliberately removed by site owner
Product discontinued or article retracted

symptoms: Page shows 'Gone' or 410 message
Old link no longer resolves

fixSteps.title: Search for replacement content
fixSteps.instruction: Use the site search or Google to find an updated or equivalent page.

fixSteps.title: Check the Wayback Machine
fixSteps.instruction: Visit web.archive.org and paste the URL to view an archived version.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable - the content is intentionally gone.

faq.a: 410 means the resource is gone permanently and intentionally; 404 means it wasn't found but might exist elsewhere or return.

title: HTTP 413 Payload Too Large
shortDescription: The request body exceeds the server's size limit.
fullDescription:
HTTP 413 Payload Too Large (formerly 'Request Entity Too Large') means the server rejected the upload because it exceeds configured size limits. Common when uploading large files, images, or videos through a web form.

Limits are set at the web server (nginx, Apache, IIS) or application layer. Typical defaults are 1-10 MB.

causes.cause: File upload exceeds server size limit
Very long form field (e.g., pasted data)

symptoms: Upload fails with 413 error
Large file posts fail while small ones succeed

fixSteps.title: Compress or resize the file
fixSteps.instruction: Use image compression, video transcoding, or ZIP to shrink the payload below the limit.

fixSteps.title: Split the upload
fixSteps.instruction: If the site supports chunked uploads, use a client that splits files.

fixSteps.title: Contact site admin
fixSteps.instruction: Ask the site to raise client_max_body_size (nginx) or equivalent.

whenToCallPro: If you run the server and need to reconfigure upload limits across the stack.

faq.a: nginx defaults to 1 MB, PHP to 2 MB. Many hosts raise to 20-100 MB for media sites.

title: HTTP 414 URI Too Long
shortDescription: The request URL exceeds the server's maximum length.
fullDescription:
HTTP 414 URI Too Long happens when the full request URL, including query string, is longer than the server allows. Typical limits are 2,000-8,000 characters. Triggered by GET forms with many fields or by encoding large data in query strings.

Switching to POST with a body usually fixes the issue.

causes.cause: Very long query string from a GET form
Recursive redirect appending parameters

symptoms: Search with many filters returns 414
Very long URL fails to load

fixSteps.title: Shorten the URL
fixSteps.instruction: Remove unnecessary query parameters, or use fewer filters.

fixSteps.title: Convert form to POST
fixSteps.instruction: Developers: switch the form method from GET to POST so data goes in the body.

whenToCallPro: If you control the app and must redesign request flow.

faq.a: Stay under 2,000 characters for maximum browser and server compatibility.

title: HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type
shortDescription: The server refuses the request because it does not support the submitted content type.
fullDescription:
HTTP 415 Unsupported Media Type means the request body's Content-Type header does not match anything the endpoint accepts. Common with REST APIs expecting application/json but receiving form-encoded data, or file uploads of the wrong MIME type.

Fix by setting the correct Content-Type header and encoding the body accordingly.

causes.cause: Wrong Content-Type header sent by client
Upload file extension not whitelisted

symptoms: API call returns 415
File upload rejected with 'unsupported media type'

fixSteps.title: Verify accepted file types
fixSteps.instruction: Check the upload form for a list of allowed extensions (PDF, PNG, etc.).

fixSteps.title: Set Content-Type header
fixSteps.instruction: Developers: ensure requests set Content-Type: application/json or multipart/form-data as appropriate.

whenToCallPro: If developing against a poorly documented API.

faq.q: Why does my JSON post return 415?
faq.a: The server likely requires Content-Type: application/json and your client is sending text/plain or form-encoded.

title: HTTP 418 I'm a teapot
shortDescription: A joke status code from an April Fools RFC, occasionally used by sites to block bots.
fullDescription:
HTTP 418 I'm a teapot was defined in RFC 2324 (Hyper Text Coffee Pot Control Protocol) as an April Fools joke. It is not a standard production status but some services use it as a non-standard way to signal that the server refuses to brew coffee - or more practically, to reject obvious bots.

Users encountering 418 in production usually hit a site that deliberately returns it.

causes.cause: Site uses 418 as a bot-detection or joke response
Cloudflare or WAF configured to return 418 for abuse

symptoms: Page shows 'I'm a teapot' message
Only some pages affected

fixSteps.title: Review your automation
fixSteps.instruction: If you are scripting requests, switch to official APIs or slow down request rate.

fixSteps.title: Contact site support
fixSteps.instruction: If you believe you are misidentified as a bot, ask the site to whitelist your IP.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable.

faq.a: It's a valid but joke HTTP status. Some services repurpose it; browsers treat it as any other 4xx.

title: HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity
shortDescription: The request body was well-formed but contains semantic errors the server cannot process.
fullDescription:
HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity means the server understood the content type and parsed the body, but validation failed - for example, a missing required field, invalid email format, or value outside allowed range.

It's distinct from 400 Bad Request, which usually signals malformed syntax. REST APIs (especially Rails, Laravel) use 422 heavily for validation failures.

causes.cause: Missing required fields in form or API call
Field values fail validation (format, range, uniqueness)

symptoms: Form submission fails with 422
API response includes validation error array

fixSteps.title: Check the response body
fixSteps.instruction: Open DevTools Network tab and inspect the 422 response - it usually lists which fields failed.

fixSteps.title: Correct the invalid fields
fixSteps.instruction: Fix the highlighted fields in the form and resubmit.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable for end users.

faq.a: 400 means the request syntax is broken; 422 means the syntax is fine but the data fails business rules.

title: HTTP 423 Locked
shortDescription: The resource is locked - usually by WebDAV or a collaborative editing system.
fullDescription:
HTTP 423 Locked is a WebDAV extension status code. It indicates the target resource is locked, typically because another user or process has it open for editing. Common in SharePoint, document collaboration tools, and WebDAV file servers.

The lock is usually released automatically after a timeout or when the other session closes the file.

causes.cause: Another user has the file open for editing
Stale lock not released after a crash

symptoms: Cannot save to shared document
WebDAV operation blocked

fixSteps.title: Wait and retry
fixSteps.instruction: Wait 1-2 minutes and try again; most locks auto-release.

fixSteps.title: Ask the other user to close the file
fixSteps.instruction: Coordinate so the current holder releases the file.

fixSteps.title: Administrator unlock
fixSteps.instruction: If lock is stale, an admin can break the lock via the server console.

whenToCallPro: For stale SharePoint/WebDAV locks requiring admin access.

faq.a: Only an administrator can break another user's lock via the WebDAV server interface.

title: HTTP 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons
shortDescription: The content is blocked due to legal demands such as court orders or government censorship.
fullDescription:
HTTP 451 Unavailable For Legal Reasons signals the server is blocking access because of a legal order - copyright takedown, court injunction, government censorship, or GDPR geographic restriction. The status code number references Ray Bradbury's novel Fahrenheit 451.

It is usually regional - content may be accessible from other countries.

causes.cause: Geographic content restriction (country blocks)
DMCA or copyright takedown
Court order removing content

symptoms: Page shows legal-reasons block
Site works from other countries
Only specific content unavailable

fixSteps.title: Check if regional
fixSteps.instruction: Try the same URL via a different network or region; some 451 blocks are geographic.

fixSteps.title: Seek alternate source
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cached or mirrored copies on web.archive.org or other legal archives.

whenToCallPro: If you own the blocked content and want to dispute the takedown - contact a media lawyer.

faq.a: No, it includes DMCA takedowns, GDPR geo-blocks, and any other legally mandated block.

title: HTTP 501 Not Implemented
shortDescription: The server does not recognize or support the functionality required to fulfill the request.
fullDescription:
HTTP 501 Not Implemented means the server cannot handle the HTTP method used (e.g., PUT or PATCH against a read-only endpoint) or feature requested. It differs from 405 Method Not Allowed, which means the method is known but not permitted on that resource.

For end users, this is typically a permanent condition until the server operator adds support.

causes.cause: HTTP method not implemented by the server
Requested feature not supported by the backend

symptoms: Specific action fails with 501
Other actions on the same site work fine

fixSteps.title: Use supported method
fixSteps.instruction: If you are a developer, consult API docs and use supported methods (GET/POST) instead.

fixSteps.title: Contact site support
fixSteps.instruction: Report the feature as missing and ask when it will be implemented.

whenToCallPro: If you are the server operator and need to implement the missing feature.

faq.a: Usually permanent until the server operator adds the missing functionality.

title: HTTP 505 HTTP Version Not Supported
shortDescription: The server does not support the HTTP protocol version used in the request.
fullDescription:
HTTP 505 HTTP Version Not Supported is returned when a client sends a request using an HTTP version the server cannot or will not process. For example, a very old server may refuse HTTP/2, or a very new server may refuse HTTP/0.9.

This is extremely rare for modern browsers, which negotiate protocol version with the server.

causes.cause: Client using outdated HTTP version
Misconfigured reverse proxy stripping HTTP version info

symptoms: Site fails with 505
Custom HTTP client gets rejected

fixSteps.title: Update your browser
fixSteps.instruction: Install the latest version of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, or Safari.

fixSteps.title: Check custom client settings
fixSteps.instruction: For curl or scripts, force HTTP/1.1 with --http1.1 flag.

whenToCallPro: If running a server or proxy that must negotiate HTTP versions.

faq.q: Can I see which HTTP version I'm using?
faq.a: DevTools Network tab shows the protocol column (h2, h3, http/1.1) for each request.

title: HTTP 508 Loop Detected
shortDescription: The server detected an infinite loop while processing the request.
fullDescription:
HTTP 508 Loop Detected, part of the WebDAV extension, signals that the server aborted because a request triggered an infinite loop. Common in WebDAV operations that recursively traverse circular references, or in reverse-proxy setups that route requests back to themselves.

End users see it mostly on SharePoint, Nextcloud, or similar file-sharing servers.

causes.cause: Circular reference in WebDAV resource tree
Reverse proxy misconfiguration routing to itself

symptoms: WebDAV action fails with 508
Sync client reports loop-detected errors

fixSteps.title: Retry outside the loop
fixSteps.instruction: Navigate manually to a different folder and operate from there.

fixSteps.title: Administrator intervention
fixSteps.instruction: Admin must remove the circular symlink or fix reverse proxy config.

whenToCallPro: Most 508 errors need server admin access to resolve.

faq.a: Only if you administer the WebDAV server or reverse proxy causing the loop.

title: Request Blocked by Ad Blocker
shortDescription: A browser extension, most often an ad blocker, blocked the request from being sent.
fullDescription:
ERR_BLOCKED_BY_CLIENT attributed to adblock means an extension (uBlock Origin, AdBlock Plus, AdGuard, Privacy Badger) intercepted and blocked the network request before it left the browser. Commonly affects ad network URLs, analytics scripts, and sometimes legitimate CDN assets whose names match blocklist patterns.

The block is client-side, so the site itself can be fine when viewed without extensions.

causes.cause: Ad blocker matches the URL against its filter list
Privacy extension blocks third-party trackers
Custom user filter accidentally blocking a legit asset

symptoms: Some requests missing from Network tab
Page partially broken with broken images or scripts
Only affected when extensions are enabled

fixSteps.title: Disable ad blocker for this site
fixSteps.instruction: Click the adblock icon in toolbar and choose 'Don't run on this site'.

fixSteps.title: Test in incognito without extensions
fixSteps.instruction: Open incognito mode with extensions disabled to confirm the block source.

fixSteps.title: Whitelist the specific domain
fixSteps.instruction: Add the blocked URL to the extension's allowlist permanently.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable.

faq.q: Should I disable my ad blocker?
faq.a: Only for trusted sites that need the blocked assets; keep it on globally for safety.

title: Generic Request Failure
shortDescription: A catch-all error when the browser can't categorize why the request failed.
fullDescription:
ERR_FAILED is Chrome's fallback error when a network request fails but the exact cause doesn't map to a more specific error. It often appears during service worker failures, CORS preflight issues, or when an extension cancels a request without a clearer signal.

Because the code is generic, diagnosing requires DevTools Network and Console tabs to find the underlying reason.

causes.cause: Service worker intercepted and failed the request
CORS preflight rejected
Extension cancelled the request silently

symptoms: Network request shows (failed) with no clearer message
Page fails to load assets intermittently

fixSteps.title: Open DevTools Console
fixSteps.instruction: Press F12, go to Console tab, and look for CORS or service worker errors for more detail.

fixSteps.title: Unregister service workers
fixSteps.instruction: In Application tab -> Service Workers, unregister workers for the site, then reload.

fixSteps.title: Disable extensions
fixSteps.instruction: Test in incognito to rule out extension interference.

whenToCallPro: If the failure is server-side and you run the backend.

faq.a: It's a catch-all when Chrome can't classify the failure; DevTools Console usually reveals the real cause.

title: Domain Name Resolution Failed
shortDescription: The browser could not resolve the domain name into an IP address through any configured resolver.
fullDescription:
ERR_NAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED is similar to ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED but covers broader DNS resolution failures, including secure DNS (DoH) provider errors and resolver misconfigurations. The browser couldn't find an IP for the requested hostname through any configured resolver.

Often temporary - caused by a flaky DNS server, VPN DNS leak protection, or a temporary glitch at your ISP.

causes.cause: DNS server is down or slow
Secure DNS (DoH) provider misconfigured
VPN DNS leak protection blocking resolution
Hosts file has stale or invalid entries

symptoms: 'This site can't be reached' with ERR_NAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED
Some domains work, others do not

fixSteps.title: Flush DNS cache
fixSteps.instruction: Open Command Prompt as admin and run: ipconfig /flushdns

fixSteps.title: Switch to Google or Cloudflare DNS
fixSteps.instruction: Network Settings -> change DNS to 8.8.8.8 / 1.1.1.1.

fixSteps.title: Disable Secure DNS temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: Chrome Settings -> Privacy and security -> Use secure DNS -> Off, then retry.

whenToCallPro: If network-wide DNS issues persist and you don't manage the router.

faq.a: ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED means the DNS query returned NXDOMAIN; ERR_NAME_RESOLUTION_FAILED covers broader resolution-layer failures.

title: Firefox: Bad Certificate Signature
shortDescription: Firefox rejected the site's TLS certificate because its cryptographic signature is invalid.
fullDescription:
SEC_ERROR_BAD_SIGNATURE indicates Firefox verified the certificate chain but the signature on one of the certificates does not match. This can happen from certificate corruption, man-in-the-middle interception, or a misconfigured server presenting a tampered cert.

Never ignore this warning - it can signal an attacker intercepting your traffic.

causes.cause: TLS interception by antivirus or corporate proxy
Corrupted certificate on the server
Active man-in-the-middle attack on network

symptoms: Firefox shows SEC_ERROR_BAD_SIGNATURE warning
Other browsers may or may not show the same error

fixSteps.title: Disable TLS-scanning in antivirus
fixSteps.instruction: In your AV (Kaspersky, Avast, ESET), turn off HTTPS / SSL scanning and retry.

fixSteps.title: Try a different network
fixSteps.instruction: Switch to mobile hotspot to confirm the issue isn't a compromised local network.

fixSteps.title: Update Firefox
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure Firefox is up to date so its crypto library is current.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists across networks and devices - could indicate targeted attack.

faq.q: Is it safe to bypass this warning?
faq.a: No. A bad signature can indicate an active attack; do not proceed.

title: Firefox: TLS Handshake Failure
shortDescription: Firefox and the server could not agree on TLS parameters during the handshake.
fullDescription:
SSL_ERROR_HANDSHAKE_FAILURE (alert 40) means the TLS handshake was aborted by the server. Common causes include the server requiring a client certificate, unsupported cipher suites, TLS version mismatches, or SNI misconfiguration.

Firefox and Chrome may behave differently because they ship different cipher lists.

causes.cause: Server requires client certificate not installed
No matching cipher suite between client and server
TLS 1.0/1.1 only server rejected by modern Firefox

symptoms: Secure connection failed in Firefox
Other browsers may succeed
Intranet or legacy sites more affected

fixSteps.title: Update Firefox
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure you're on the latest Firefox for updated cipher support.

fixSteps.title: Check for required client cert
fixSteps.instruction: For corporate sites, confirm you've imported the required personal certificate in Firefox options.

fixSteps.title: Test in about:config
fixSteps.instruction: Check security.tls.version.min and adjust only if instructed by IT.

whenToCallPro: If server is internal and handshake negotiation needs server-side fix.

faq.a: Firefox uses NSS with its own cipher list; handshake may fail differently than Chrome's BoringSSL.

title: Firefox: No Common Cipher with Server
shortDescription: Firefox and the server have no cipher suite in common, so TLS cannot be established.
fullDescription:
SSL_ERROR_NO_CYPHER_OVERLAP appears when Firefox's supported cipher suites don't overlap with the server's. Modern Firefox no longer supports RC4, 3DES, and other legacy ciphers, so old servers that only offer these will fail.

The sustainable fix is for the server to be upgraded. Temporary workarounds exist in about:config but weaken security.

causes.cause: Server only supports deprecated ciphers (RC4, 3DES)
Server running very old TLS library

symptoms: Secure connection failed
Site loads in older browsers but not Firefox
Legacy devices (routers, printers) affected

fixSteps.title: Ask admin to update server TLS
fixSteps.instruction: Report the site to its operator so they can enable modern cipher suites.

fixSteps.title: Use a different browser temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: For legacy local devices, use a dedicated old browser rather than weakening Firefox settings.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the server and need to upgrade TLS configuration.

faq.a: Technically yes via about:config, but it seriously weakens security - avoid unless absolutely necessary.

title: Firefox: Connection Reset by Peer
shortDescription: Firefox's Netscape Portable Runtime (NSPR) reports that the TCP connection was reset by the server.
fullDescription:
PR_CONNECT_RESET_ERROR is Firefox's equivalent of Chrome's ERR_CONNECTION_RESET. The server or an intermediate device sent a TCP RST, terminating the connection mid-flight. Causes range from firewalls dropping idle connections to DDoS protections rejecting your IP.

Typically transient. If persistent, a network device between you and the server is deliberately killing the connection.

causes.cause: Firewall or DPI device resets connection
Server overloaded and closing connections abruptly
Antivirus HTTPS scanning interfering

symptoms: 'The connection was reset' page in Firefox
Other browsers may show ERR_CONNECTION_RESET

fixSteps.title: Reload the page
fixSteps.instruction: Retry the URL - transient resets often clear up.

fixSteps.title: Disable HTTPS scanning
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off antivirus TLS inspection temporarily to see if it resolves.

fixSteps.title: Try a different network
fixSteps.instruction: Switch to mobile hotspot to rule out local firewall issues.

whenToCallPro: If the reset comes from corporate firewall and needs IT policy change.

faq.a: Connection was aborted before completion; no sensitive data was sent if the reset occurred early in handshake.

title: Firefox: Unexpected End of Connection
shortDescription: Firefox hit an unexpected end-of-stream while reading from the server.
fullDescription:
PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR means Firefox (via NSPR) was reading a response when the connection closed unexpectedly without the expected TLS close_notify. Commonly tied to proxies, firewalls, or servers that abruptly terminate TLS.

It is similar to ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE in Chrome.

causes.cause: Proxy or gateway drops the connection early
Server crashes mid-response
Aggressive antivirus TLS inspection

symptoms: 'Secure Connection Failed' with PR_END_OF_FILE_ERROR
Reload sometimes fixes it

fixSteps.title: Retry the request
fixSteps.instruction: Refresh to see if the issue is transient.

fixSteps.title: Disable antivirus TLS scan
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off HTTPS scanning to test.

fixSteps.title: Bypass proxy
fixSteps.instruction: Temporarily disable any configured proxy in OS or Firefox settings.

whenToCallPro: If the server consistently fails and you administer it.

faq.q: Does this mean the site is hacked?
faq.a: Not necessarily - usually a proxy or antivirus is interrupting the connection.

title: Firefox: OCSP Response Missing for Certificate
shortDescription: Firefox could not verify the certificate's revocation status because the OCSP response was missing.
fullDescription:
MOZILLA_PKIX_ERROR_OCSP_RESPONSE_FOR_CERT_MISSING is raised when Firefox performs an OCSP check (or uses stapled OCSP) but the response for the certificate was absent. Firefox can be configured to hard-fail on missing OCSP - if the OCSP server is unreachable, the page will be blocked.

Common when OCSP stapling is misconfigured on the server, or when the client network blocks OCSP endpoints.

causes.cause: Server's OCSP stapling misconfigured
Client network blocks OCSP URLs
OCSP responder temporarily down

symptoms: Firefox blocks HTTPS site with OCSP error
Other browsers may load the site fine

fixSteps.title: Retry after a minute
fixSteps.instruction: OCSP responders have brief outages - retry soon.

fixSteps.title: Try different network
fixSteps.instruction: Some corporate firewalls block OCSP; test from home or mobile hotspot.

fixSteps.title: Adjust OCSP settings (advanced)
fixSteps.instruction: In about:config, temporarily set security.OCSP.require to false - lowers security.

whenToCallPro: If you own the server and need to fix OCSP stapling configuration.

faq.q: Should I turn off OCSP checks?
faq.a: No - OCSP is how Firefox detects revoked certificates. Disable only temporarily for diagnostics.

title: Safari: Blob Resource Loading Error
shortDescription: Safari failed to load a Blob or media resource from memory, often during video playback.
fullDescription:
WebKitBlobResource error 1 commonly appears in Safari's console when a video or audio element tries to load from a Blob URL that has already been revoked or is inaccessible. Typical triggers include Media Source Extensions (MSE) streaming errors, aggressive power-saving on macOS, or seeking past available buffer.

Users experience it as videos that refuse to play or stop mid-stream.

causes.cause: Blob URL revoked before playback completed
MSE streaming buffer issue
macOS Low Power Mode throttling

symptoms: Video fails to play in Safari
Playback stalls and never resumes
Console shows 'WebKitBlobResource error 1'

fixSteps.title: Disable Low Power Mode
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings -> Battery -> turn off Low Power Mode.

fixSteps.title: Clear Safari website data
fixSteps.instruction: Safari -> Settings -> Privacy -> Manage Website Data -> Remove All.

fixSteps.title: Try a different browser
fixSteps.instruction: Test the video in Chrome or Firefox to confirm it's Safari-specific.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable for end users.

faq.a: Safari's media stack enforces Blob URL lifetimes strictly; Chrome and Firefox are more lenient.

title: Safari: Request Timed Out
shortDescription: Safari's URL loading system reports the request took too long and was cancelled.
fullDescription:
NSURLErrorDomain -1001 (NSURLErrorTimedOut) on macOS and iOS Safari indicates the request exceeded its timeout budget. The TCP connection may have stalled, the server may be very slow, or the network is congested.

It is the Safari equivalent of ERR_CONNECTION_TIMED_OUT.

causes.cause: Slow or congested network
Server very slow to respond
VPN or proxy adding latency

symptoms: Safari shows 'The request timed out'
Only some sites affected
Works on other devices on the same network

fixSteps.title: Retry the page
fixSteps.instruction: Tap reload - transient latency often clears.

fixSteps.title: Toggle Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: Turn Wi-Fi off and back on to re-establish the connection.

fixSteps.title: Disable VPN
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off VPN temporarily to see if the timeout originates there.

whenToCallPro: Persistent timeouts on a managed network needing IT review.

faq.a: Default is 60 seconds but apps can adjust it; the 60-second ceiling is typical for web loads.

title: Safari: A server with the specified hostname could not be found
shortDescription: Safari could not resolve the hostname to an IP address.
fullDescription:
NSURLErrorDomain -1003 (NSURLErrorCannotFindHost) means DNS resolution failed - the hostname does not resolve to any IP. This is Safari's counterpart to ERR_NAME_NOT_RESOLVED.

Caused by typos in the URL, DNS outages, or network configuration issues.

causes.cause: Typo in the URL or stale bookmark
DNS server outage
VPN blocking DNS

symptoms: 'Cannot find server' page
Works on mobile data but not Wi-Fi or vice versa

fixSteps.title: Verify the URL
fixSteps.instruction: Double-check spelling of the domain.

fixSteps.title: Change DNS
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings -> Network -> Wi-Fi -> Details -> DNS -> set to 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8.

fixSteps.title: Restart router
fixSteps.instruction: Power-cycle the router if issue is network-wide.

whenToCallPro: Persistent DNS issues on corporate networks.

faq.q: Why does Safari report -1003 but Chrome works?
faq.a: They may use different DNS caches; try clearing system DNS cache with 'sudo dscacheutil -flushcache'.

title: Safari: Could Not Connect to the Server
shortDescription: Safari reached the DNS but failed to open a TCP connection to the server.
fullDescription:
NSURLErrorDomain -1004 (NSURLErrorCannotConnectToHost) means DNS resolved but the subsequent TCP connect attempt failed. Server may be down, port blocked, or local firewall rejecting outgoing traffic.

Similar to ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED in Chrome.

causes.cause: Server is down or not listening on the port
Firewall blocking the port
Local proxy misconfigured

symptoms: 'Safari cannot open the page because it could not connect to the server'
Works from other networks

fixSteps.title: Retry after a minute
fixSteps.instruction: Server may be rebooting.

fixSteps.title: Check firewall settings
fixSteps.instruction: System Settings -> Network -> Firewall - temporarily disable to test.

fixSteps.title: Disable proxy
fixSteps.instruction: Network -> Proxies -> uncheck all boxes and retry.

whenToCallPro: If server-side outage requires vendor involvement.

faq.q: Is this a server or client problem?
faq.a: Either - try from another device/network to narrow it down.

title: HTTP 421 Misdirected Request
shortDescription: The server received a request not intended for it, typically due to HTTP/2 connection coalescing.
fullDescription:
HTTP 421 Misdirected Request means the server received a request on a connection that is not configured to produce responses for the requested authority. This most often occurs with HTTP/2 connection coalescing, where a browser reuses a TLS connection for a different hostname that happens to share the IP and certificate.

It's a signal for the browser to open a new connection and retry.

causes.cause: HTTP/2 connection coalescing with different virtual host
Load balancer routing quirks

symptoms: Sporadic 421 errors
Issue clears on reload

fixSteps.title: Reload the page
fixSteps.instruction: Browser will open a new dedicated connection and retry.

fixSteps.title: Disable HTTP/2 coalescing (advanced)
fixSteps.instruction: Server admin: ensure certs and SNI configs don't invite coalescing for unrelated hosts.

whenToCallPro: If you run the server and 421 is frequent for users.

faq.q: Is 421 a server or browser bug?
faq.a: Neither - it's a protocol-level signal to open a fresh connection; browsers handle it automatically.

title: HTTP 425 Too Early
shortDescription: The server refuses to process the request sent in TLS early-data to prevent replay attacks.
fullDescription:
HTTP 425 Too Early is returned when a server does not want to risk processing a request that may have been replayed using TLS 1.3 0-RTT (zero round-trip time) early data. The client should retry after the TLS handshake completes.

Mostly invisible to end users - modern browsers retry automatically.

causes.cause: Server rejected 0-RTT data to avoid replay

symptoms: Rare, mostly transparent to users
Visible in DevTools Network tab

fixSteps.title: Let the browser retry
fixSteps.instruction: Modern browsers automatically retry after the full handshake.

whenToCallPro: Not applicable.

faq.a: Yes, it's specific to 0-RTT early data in TLS 1.3.

title: HTTP 426 Upgrade Required
shortDescription: The server requires the client to switch to a different protocol, such as HTTPS or HTTP/2.
fullDescription:
HTTP 426 Upgrade Required tells the client it must use a different protocol. The response includes an Upgrade header naming the required protocol (e.g., TLS/1.3 or WebSocket). Servers commonly return 426 when HTTP/1.1 is no longer allowed.

Modern browsers rarely see 426 because they typically negotiate TLS and HTTP/2 by default.

causes.cause: Server requires HTTPS upgrade
API expects WebSocket upgrade

symptoms: Legacy client fails with 426
API call returns upgrade required

fixSteps.title: Use HTTPS URL
fixSteps.instruction: Change http:// to https:// in your URL and retry.

fixSteps.title: Update your client library
fixSteps.instruction: Developers: update the HTTP/TLS library to a version supporting the required protocol.

whenToCallPro: If updating a legacy embedded client that can't speak the newer protocol.

faq.q: Why does my old script get 426?
faq.a: It's probably using HTTP/1.0 or plain HTTP against a server that now requires TLS.

displayCode: HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
title: HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large
shortDescription: The server refuses to process the request because its headers (e.g., cookies) are too large.
fullDescription:
HTTP 431 Request Header Fields Too Large is returned when the combined size of request headers - especially cookies - exceeds the server's limit. Typical limits are 8KB per header and 16-32KB total.

Fixing involves trimming cookies or other headers. Clearing site cookies usually resolves the issue immediately.

causes.cause: Cookies from many extensions or sessions accumulated
Overly large custom headers set by code

symptoms: Page fails with 431 after long session
Clearing cookies fixes it

fixSteps.title: Clear cookies for the site
fixSteps.instruction: DevTools -> Application -> Cookies -> select domain -> Clear.

fixSteps.title: Try incognito
fixSteps.instruction: Open the site in a private window with no cookies.

fixSteps.title: Trim custom headers
fixSteps.instruction: Developers: shrink Authorization tokens or move state into request body.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Nginx and Apache default to 8 KB per header and 8-16 KB total; some CDNs are stricter.

title: HTTP 506 Variant Also Negotiates
shortDescription: Server-side content negotiation is misconfigured and produces a circular reference.
fullDescription:
HTTP 506 Variant Also Negotiates indicates a server configuration error where a selected variant is itself configured to engage in content negotiation, causing a loop. Extremely rare in practice; only appears on servers using transparent content negotiation (TCN).

Fix is server-side only.

causes.cause: Misconfigured TCN on Apache server

symptoms: Rare - typically seen by server admins during debugging

fixSteps.title: Contact site admin
fixSteps.instruction: Report the URL - this error requires server-side reconfiguration.

whenToCallPro: Almost always - this is a server configuration bug.

faq.a: No - only the site owner can fix the configuration.

title: HTTP 510 Not Extended
shortDescription: The server requires further extensions to the request before it can be fulfilled.
fullDescription:
HTTP 510 Not Extended comes from RFC 2774 and indicates the server needs additional extension headers to fulfill the request. Rare and mostly obsolete, but some enterprise APIs still emit it.

End users can't typically fix it.

causes.cause: Enterprise API demands HTTP extension framework

symptoms: API call fails with 510

fixSteps.title: Consult API docs
fixSteps.instruction: Check vendor documentation for required extension headers.

whenToCallPro: Typically required - most 510 errors need API vendor support.

faq.a: No - it's used by a narrow set of enterprise systems.

title: SSL Server Certificate Has Bad Format
shortDescription: The server's TLS certificate is malformed and cannot be parsed by the browser.
fullDescription:
ERR_SSL_SERVER_CERT_BAD_FORMAT means the browser received a certificate during TLS handshake that it cannot parse - usually a DER/PEM encoding error, wrong ASN.1 structure, or truncated chain. The site owner must re-issue or reconfigure the certificate.

Users cannot bypass this safely; do not click 'proceed anyway'.

causes.cause: Server admin installed a truncated or corrupted cert
Incorrect cert chain concatenation

symptoms: Page blocked with cert bad format warning
Other browsers may show different cert errors

fixSteps.title: Report to site owner
fixSteps.instruction: Contact the site's support and mention the cert format error.

fixSteps.title: Use alternate access
fixSteps.instruction: If available, use the site's mobile app or a different domain.

whenToCallPro: If you manage the server, work with your CA to re-issue the certificate.

faq.a: No - a malformed cert is a sign of serious misconfiguration; wait for the site owner to fix it.

title: HTTP Response Code Failure
shortDescription: Chrome received an HTTP response code that triggered a network-layer failure.
fullDescription:
ERR_HTTP_RESPONSE_CODE_FAILURE appears in Chrome when the server returns a status code the networking stack treats as a failure, typically in contexts like Signed HTTP Exchanges, prefetch, or subresource integrity flows.

Rare in everyday browsing; usually encountered by developers working with advanced features.

causes.cause: Signed HTTP Exchange validation failure
Prefetch hint mismatched status code

symptoms: Resource fails to load with this code
Prefetch or SXG errors in DevTools

fixSteps.title: Reload without prefetch
fixSteps.instruction: Hard reload (Ctrl+F5) to bypass prefetch hints.

fixSteps.title: Developers: inspect response
fixSteps.instruction: Use DevTools to inspect the exact status code and headers returned.

whenToCallPro: If you operate the server and need SXG or prefetch correctness.

faq.a: No - mostly seen in advanced networking scenarios like prefetch or SXG.

title: Socket Read Error
shortDescription: Chrome failed while reading data from the network socket mid-transfer.
fullDescription:
ERR_SOCKET_READ_ERROR signals that a low-level read from the TCP socket failed while the response was still arriving. Possible causes include network interface flaps, VPN tunnel drops, system sleep interrupting the transfer, or firewall killing the connection.

Usually recoverable with a reload.

causes.cause: Network interface flapped (Wi-Fi, Ethernet)
VPN disconnected mid-transfer
Firewall terminated the socket

symptoms: Page fails partway through load
Reload usually succeeds

fixSteps.title: Reload
fixSteps.instruction: Press Ctrl+R to retry the request.

fixSteps.title: Check connection stability
fixSteps.instruction: Move closer to router, plug in Ethernet, or switch Wi-Fi band.

fixSteps.title: Disable VPN temporarily
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off VPN to see if it's the source of drops.

whenToCallPro: Persistent read errors on a managed/corporate network.

faq.q: Is this the same as connection reset?
faq.a: Close - connection reset is a TCP RST; socket read error is a lower-level read failure with broader causes.

title: Edge STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION
shortDescription: Edge tab crashes with STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION (0xC0000005).
fullDescription: Edge (Chromium) displays STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION on the error page when a renderer tried to access invalid memory. Causes include a faulty extension, corrupt user profile, outdated GPU driver, or injected third-party DLL (security software).

causes.cause: Faulty extension
Injected third-party DLL (AV)
Outdated GPU driver
Corrupt user data folder

symptoms: 'Aw, Snap!' style crash page in Edge
Multiple tabs die simultaneously

fixSteps.title: Disable extensions
fixSteps.instruction: edge://extensions > toggle off all.

fixSteps.title: Toggle hardware acceleration
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > Use hardware acceleration - flip it.

fixSteps.title: Clear profile
fixSteps.instruction: Create new Edge profile and test.

fixSteps.title: Update/reinstall Edge
fixSteps.instruction: edge://settings/help then reinstall if needed.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

title: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN
shortDescription: Chromium-based browser tab crash — stack buffer corruption detected.
fullDescription: STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN (0xC0000409) is triggered by /GS stack cookie mismatch. For browsers this almost always means a compatibility shim or injected DLL (antivirus, Nahimic, Riot Vanguard) is conflicting with the renderer.

causes.cause: Third-party DLL injection
Corrupt extension manifest
Outdated browser version

symptoms: Tab crash with this status on error page
Reloading often continues

fixSteps.title: Enable Chrome Cleanup / scan for injected DLLs
fixSteps.instruction: Use Process Explorer, verify loaded modules under chrome.exe.

fixSteps.title: Update browser
fixSteps.instruction: About > update, relaunch.

fixSteps.title: Disable extensions
fixSteps.instruction: Disable all, re-enable one at a time.

whenToCallPro: If DLL injection is from required corporate software.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

title: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH
shortDescription: Browser refuses to load a DLL due to integrity check failure.
fullDescription: STATUS_INVALID_IMAGE_HASH (0xC0000428) means Windows Code Integrity rejected a DLL signature. Common with out-of-date Chromium versions against patched Windows Code Integrity, or when AV has altered a DLL on disk.

causes.cause: Outdated browser against new Windows build
AV has quarantined/modified a DLL
Corrupted download

symptoms: Tab crash page with this status
Starts after a Windows feature update

fixSteps.title: Update browser
fixSteps.instruction: chrome://settings/help - update to latest.

fixSteps.title: Check AV quarantine
fixSteps.instruction: Review quarantined items, restore if legitimate.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall browser
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall, delete user data, reinstall.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

title: Netflix Error M7353-5101
shortDescription: Netflix detects an unsupported browser extension.
fullDescription: Netflix error M7353-5101 appears when a browser extension interferes with Widevine DRM playback. Typical culprits: ad blockers, VPN extensions, script blockers, or user-agent spoofers.

causes.cause: Ad blocker or privacy extension
VPN extension blocking DRM
Hardware acceleration off

symptoms: Error overlay on Netflix player
Other streaming sites work

fixSteps.instruction: Extensions > disable on this site.

fixSteps.title: Try incognito/InPrivate
fixSteps.instruction: No extensions loaded.

fixSteps.title: Enable hardware acceleration
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > System > enable acceleration.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

fullDescription: P-DEV318 is a Hulu playback failure often tied to server load, stale cache, or account sync issues. Clearing cookies and restarting usually resolves it.

Hulu server incident
Concurrent stream limit

symptoms: Play button spins then errors P-DEV318
Home screen loads but no video

fixSteps.instruction: Ends extra sessions and refreshes tokens.

title: YouTube Network Error (400)
shortDescription: 'There was a problem with the network. (Error Code: 400)' on YouTube.
fullDescription: YouTube 400 indicates a malformed request to YouTube servers, usually caused by a corrupted cookie, stale auth token, or misbehaving extension modifying headers.

Extension modifying Host header
Wrong date/time

symptoms: Player error 400
Problem happens after extended session

fixSteps.instruction: Site settings > clear data.

fixSteps.instruction: Enable auto time.

Outdated Widevine CDM

Other streaming services still work

title: Disney+ Error 83

fullDescription: Disney+ error 83 means a compatibility issue: unsupported browser, device, or network configuration. Often triggered by VPN use, older browsers, or corporate networks.

VPN active
Weak network connection

Content won't start

fixSteps.instruction: Ensure a current supported browser.

Network interruption
Browser extension interfering

'Connection lost' banner

whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

title: Cookie Policy Violation (SameSite)
shortDescription: Cookie not set/sent because SameSite or Secure policy violated.
fullDescription: Modern browsers reject cookies without SameSite or those set cross-origin without Secure+SameSite=None. DevTools Issues tab shows clear warnings for developers; end users see broken logins and session loss.

Secure flag missing over HTTPS-only policy

symptoms: Intermittent logouts
DevTools 'This Set-Cookie was blocked' warnings

fixSteps.title: Developer fix
fixSteps.instruction: Set SameSite=None; Secure for cross-site cookies.

fixSteps.title: User workaround

whenToCallPro: Never for end users.

faq.a: Usually resolvable with browser troubleshooting.

title: Safari SSL Error
shortDescription: Safari reports NSURLErrorDomain -1200 when the SSL/TLS handshake fails.
fullDescription: An underlying CFNetwork SSL error was raised while loading the page in Safari on macOS. Most commonly triggered by expired server certificates, outdated macOS trust store, or broken Keychain certificate entries.

causes.cause: Misconfigured Safari setup on the remote server
Browser cache or profile corruption
Extension or enterprise security product interfering
Outdated browser or operating system

symptoms: DevTools Console shows NSURLErrorDomain -1200
Page fails to load or a specific resource is missing
Error reproduces in normal mode but not in a fresh profile
Other browsers may or may not show the same error

fixSteps.title: Reproduce with DevTools open
fixSteps.instruction: Open DevTools (F12 / Cmd+Opt+I) and reload the page. Check the Console and Network tabs for the exact failing request.

fixSteps.title: Clear browser cache
fixSteps.instruction: Clear cached data for the affected site (Settings > Privacy > Clear browsing data, or Cmd+Shift+Delete).

fixSteps.title: Try a fresh profile or Private window
fixSteps.instruction: Open a Private/Incognito window to test without extensions. If the error goes away, disable extensions one by one.

fixSteps.title: Update the browser and OS
fixSteps.instruction: Install the latest browser update and any pending macOS/Windows updates to refresh the TLS/CORS stack.

fixSteps.title: Contact the site owner if the server is at fault
fixSteps.instruction: If the issue is CORS or server configuration, share the failing request and response headers with the site's operator.

whenToCallPro: If the error only affects your enterprise network or a corporate site, escalate to your IT/help desk — the server or proxy configuration is usually at fault.

faq.q: Is NSURLErrorDomain -1200 caused by my browser?
faq.a: Often partly — but server configuration, extensions, and OS-level trust stores all contribute. Use the steps above to narrow down the source.
Only if profile corruption or a bad extension is the cause. Test a fresh profile first before reinstalling.

fullDescription: Indicates a renderer process hit a debug breakpoint, usually after a bad extension, corrupt profile, or Memory integrity conflict in Core Isolation.

causes.cause: Misconfigured Edge setup on the remote server
Browser cache or profile corruption
Extension or enterprise security product interfering
Outdated browser or operating system

symptoms: DevTools Console shows STATUS_BREAKPOINT (Edge)
Page fails to load or a specific resource is missing
Error reproduces in normal mode but not in a fresh profile
Other browsers may or may not show the same error

fixSteps.title: Reproduce with DevTools open
fixSteps.instruction: Open DevTools (F12 / Cmd+Opt+I) and reload the page. Check the Console and Network tabs for the exact failing request.

fixSteps.title: Clear browser cache
fixSteps.instruction: Clear cached data for the affected site (Settings > Privacy > Clear browsing data, or Cmd+Shift+Delete).

fixSteps.title: Try a fresh profile or Private window
fixSteps.instruction: Open a Private/Incognito window to test without extensions. If the error goes away, disable extensions one by one.

fixSteps.title: Update the browser and OS
fixSteps.instruction: Install the latest browser update and any pending macOS/Windows updates to refresh the TLS/CORS stack.

fixSteps.title: Contact the site owner if the server is at fault
fixSteps.instruction: If the issue is CORS or server configuration, share the failing request and response headers with the site's operator.

whenToCallPro: If the error only affects your enterprise network or a corporate site, escalate to your IT/help desk — the server or proxy configuration is usually at fault.

faq.q: Is STATUS_BREAKPOINT (Edge) caused by my browser?
faq.a: Often partly — but server configuration, extensions, and OS-level trust stores all contribute. Use the steps above to narrow down the source.
Only if profile corruption or a bad extension is the cause. Test a fresh profile first before reinstalling.
